old_caption:
The video captures a serene backyard scene on a clear day. The focal point is a wooden fence that runs horizontally across the frame, separating the viewer's perspective from the yard beyond. A small patch of grass is visible through the fence, and a few trees with sparse leaves suggest it might be late autumn or early spring. In the background, a house with a gray roof is partially visible, nestled among more trees.

As the video progresses, a noticeable change occurs: steam begins to rise from the left side of the frame, billowing upwards and drifting across the yard. The steam appears thick and white at first but gradually disperses into thin wisps, revealing the clear blue sky above. The sun casts a warm glow over the entire scene, enhancing the tranquil atmosphere. The camera remains stationary throughout, focusing on the fence and the evolving steam, providing a steady view of the backyard's peaceful setting.

caption:
The video captures a backyard on a bright, cold morning. A dark wooden picket fence runs across the foreground, its light orange-brown gate post left of center. Behind it, a frost-covered lawn holds a clothesline, a small leafy shrub on the right, and two dark round objects on the grass. A taller gray privacy fence encloses the yard, beyond which sit a shingled roof, string lights, evergreen and bare trees, and strong sun glare.

Throughout the clip, white mist rises behind the left part of the foreground fence, a thin veil trailing along its top. As the camera pans to the left, the scene slides rightward across the frame, the light gate post drifting toward the center. Relative to the fence, the horizontal veil continues along the top, while the billowing column on the left persists and shifts shape. A separate small puff near the top of the privacy-fence corner shifts rightward with the scene, and the sun glare and clothesline remain present.

endpoints are normal, not physical errors. Do not add unseen causes, onset, stopping or outcomes.
An internal editing cut is not evidence of physical motion connecting the views.

Check identification before physical interpretation: a reflection is not a separate actor;
a powder/smoke/liquid outline or shadow is not automatically the boundary of a solid object;
an apparent change caused by occlusion/viewpoint is not automatically material deformation.
Do not claim contact, bending, compression, melting, disintegration or structural recovery unless
the appropriate material/surface itself provides visible evidence. Do not infer a force or earlier
collision just because the visible configuration would be compatible with it.
Compare several frames before asserting translation, rotation, direction, unchanged position or
camera tracking. A single visible texture/seam does not prove spin. Avoid unnecessary absolute
claims of stillness, no motion, no camera motion or 'exactly' synchronized changes.
Remove invented scene details and explanations, but keep clearly visible ongoing motion and
processes. Avoid deleting the real process merely because its cause lies outside the cropped window.

Retain the WISA English narrative style, detail density and paragraph structure. Aim for the
provided original word count within 85%-115%, using genuinely visible details and process.
Do not add repetition, watermark/logo descriptions or atmospheric filler to reach a word count.

'this mid-segment', 'the excerpt', 'the frame', 'these images', 'observed evidence' in the caption.
This is a direct video description, not an analysis note. No mandatory beginning/end formula.
Complete every sentence. If accuracy requires a substantial length difference, explain it outside
the caption; do not fill missing context by imagination. Optional synonym edits are not needed.

draft_caption:
The video captures a backyard on a bright, cold morning. A dark wooden picket fence runs across the foreground, its light orange-brown gate post left of center. Behind it, a frost-covered lawn holds a clothesline, a small leafy shrub on the right, and two dark round objects on the grass. A taller gray privacy fence encloses the yard, beyond which sit a shingled roof, string lights, evergreen and bare trees, and strong sun glare.

Throughout the clip, white mist rises behind the left part of the foreground fence, a thin veil trailing along its top. As the camera pans to the left, the whole scene slides steadily rightward across the frame, the light gate post drifting toward the center. Relative to the fence, the horizontal veil lengthens toward the right, while the billowing column on the left persists and shifts shape. A separate small puff near the top of the privacy-fence corner stays roughly fixed, and the sun glare and clothesline remain present.

review_issues.quote: the whole scene slides steadily rightward across the frame
review_issues.problem: The visible motion is rightward, but 'whole' and 'steadily' overstate the evidence; the frames show a scene sliding rightward without proof that every element moves as one rigid whole or at constant speed.

review_issues.quote: Relative to the fence, the horizontal veil lengthens toward the right
review_issues.problem: The veil's extent relative to the fence does not visibly lengthen; it continues along the fence top while the camera pans, so the lengthening claim is unsupported.

review_issues.quote: A separate small puff near the top of the privacy-fence corner stays roughly fixed
review_issues.problem: The puff shifts rightward in the frame with the rest of the scene because of the leftward camera motion; it only remains near the corner, so 'stays roughly fixed' is misleading.
